title: Lithuania Faces Twin Pressures of Persistent Inflation and Security Anxiety… · 05 Sep
keywords: Lithuania, inflation, European Commission, tax reform, property tax, environmental tax, fossil fuel subsidies, eurozone, Russia, security, NATO, Baltic states, espionage, drones, fiscal policy, EU governance, Kaliningrad, defence spending
notes: Lithuania is navigating a difficult convergence of elevated inflation, EU demands for tax reform, and an intensifying security threat environment on NATO's eastern flank. With annual inflation running at 5.4 percent in July 2026, among the highest in the eurozone, the government faces resistance to Brussels-backed fiscal changes that critics say will squeeze households already under financial pressure. At the same time, espionage cases and concerns over Russian drone activity are keeping the national mood tense and the defence budget under strain. The two pressures together define a central challenge for Vilnius: how to fund resilience without exhausting public trust.
